title: Should the Fouled Player Take the Penalty Himself?
excerpt: A player gets fouled by the GK and walks straight to the spot. Should he? Theory says no — jarred, agitated, while the keeper is locked in. A one-tailed z-test on 100 treatment cases vs 3,757 controls in the top 5 European leagues.
finding: When the fouled player takes the penalty himself, conversion drops 3.25 pp (75.0% vs 78.25%) — but with only 100 such cases the data can't yet say 'hand it to someone else' (p = 0.22, one-tailed).

title: Not All Goals Are Equal: A Time-Aware Expected-Points Model
excerpt: A goal from 0–0 to 1–0 in the fifth minute and the same goal in the eighty-fifth are not the same thing. Expected points (EP) prices every goal by the goal-difference transition it produced and the minute it landed — across 39,381 goals in six top-flight leagues and seven seasons.
finding: A late equaliser is worth 2.1× an early opener — and Mário Rui collects more late points than anyone.
